Coquitlam condos for sale: apartment-style homes in strata buildings. The Greater Vancouver REALTORS® benchmark for apartments (condos) in Coquitlam was $640,100 in September 2026 (-7.3% over a year). Before you offer, read the strata documents: the depreciation report, meeting minutes, bylaws and fees.
Coquitlam condos sold, November 2025 to October 2026

768 condos sold in Coquitlam with a median price of $613,450 (the middle half sold between $505,750 and $705,000), taking a median of 24 days to sell at 97.4% of the last list price; 6% sold above list. They had a median $769 per square foot, a median year built of 2015 and a median strata fee of $432 a month.

Coquitlam Condos: streets and boundaries

items.t: Coquitlam's condo stock sits in three different transit corridors, not one downtown: City Centre on Pinetree Way and Barnet Highway, Burquitlam and Lougheed on North Road, and the low-rise benches above them — and the City's own growth plan splits those corridors from the existing neighbourhoods.

The City states new growth is focused in transit-oriented areas near SkyTrain, such as City Centre, Burquitlam and Lougheed, taking 50% of growth, and in existing neighbourhoods such as Austin Heights and Maillardville, taking 29% of growth.

blocks.text: Coquitlam Condos: the housing stock

items.t: The Burquitlam Capital on North Road is a named city condo building whose own developer page records 189 condominiums plus four townhomes — 193 homes in total — which is the counting method a buyer should use when a building source gives a different total.

The City's current building-permit list shows the form range being added now: a single new six-storey apartment building of 94 units at 727 North Road, in the application stream August 17, 2026, at the low-rise end, against the City Centre and Burquitlam towers at the high end.
The same City list shows townhouse-form product still being permitted inside the city: construction of 16 townhouses at 3469 Baycrest Avenue, in the application stream August 19, 2026.
Strata versus freehold and rental or pet bylaws are building-by-building in Coquitlam and are not stated on a City page; they come from each building's Form B and strata bylaws.

blocks.text: Coquitlam Condos: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Coquitlam's zoning is Zoning Bylaw No.

The Southwest Shoulders and Corridors amendments, adopted May 27, 2026, updated land use around the Burquitlam and Lougheed Town Centre SkyTrain stations and along Austin Avenue, creating opportunities for medium-density housing and townhousing in Southwest Coquitlam.

blocks.text: Coquitlam Condos: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The City expects 90,000 new residents over the next 25 years, as stated on its How Development Happens page — the demand backdrop behind the City Centre and Burquitlam tower pipeline a condo buyer is purchasing beside.

A rezoning of 374 properties in the Southwest Shoulder and Corridor sub-areas, from R-3 Transitional Small-Scale Residential to R-1 Small-Scale Residential under Zoning Amendment Bylaw No. 5522, 2026, was before Council on July 6, 2026 — a live zoning change beside existing Southwest Coquitlam condos.
Coquitlam's 2026 budget raised property tax by $93 a year for the average household (3.37%), and by $137 a year with utilities included, as stated in the City's December 9, 2025 budget release.

To find the land-use designation of a specific condo-adjacent property, the City directs residents to its QtheMap viewer or to DevInfo@coquitlam.ca, as stated on the Transit-Oriented Areas project page.

blocks.text: Coquitlam Condos: getting around

items.t: Coquitlam Central Station is the city's rail hub, served by the Millennium Line Evergreen Extension and the West Coast Express, and is the terminus named on the TransLink timetables for routes 153, 185, 186 and 187 that feed the condo corridors.
Route 153 links the city's two SkyTrain ends, running Braid Station to Coquitlam Central Station via Brunette Avenue, Austin Avenue, Poirier Street, Como Lake Avenue and Mariner Way.
Route 187 runs Coquitlam Central Station to Parkway via Johnson Street, Plateau Boulevard and Paddock Drive, serving the Westwood Plateau low-rise stock.

blocks.text: Coquitlam Condos: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check flood siting under Zoning Bylaw No.

Check the City's floodplain mapping report for the Coquitlam, Fraser and Pitt rivers before buying near a river edge; the report is the City's mapping work, not a lot-level flood determination for a specific strata lot.

Check Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) status per parcel on Agricultural Land Commission mapping for any land or new-build purchase at the city edge; no ALR clearance for a specific parcel is given here.

blocks.text: Jared's take on Coquitlam

In Coquitlam, buyers sort by pocket, school and commute, because each part of the city is its own market. The southwest side is planned around the Burquitlam and Lougheed Town Centre station areas and Austin Avenue.

faq.q: What did condos in Coquitlam sell for?
faq.a: 768 condos sold in Coquitlam between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $613,450.

faq.q: How long do condos take to sell in Coquitlam?
faq.a: The median was 24 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.4% of the last list price (6% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: What price range do most condos in Coquitlam sell in?
faq.a: The middle half of the 768 condos that sold in Coquitlam went for between $505,750 and $705,000, around a median of $613,450.

faq.q: Do condos in Coquitlam sell above asking price?
faq.a: 6% of the 768 condos sold for more than the last list price, and the median sale was 97.4% of it.

faq.q: What is a typical strata fee for condos in Coquitlam?
faq.a: Of the 768 sales, 767 listings gave a monthly fee and the median was $432.

faq.q: How old are the condos that sold in Coquitlam?
faq.a: The median year built was 2015 for the 768 condos sold in Coquitlam.

faq.q: How many bedrooms do condos in Coquitlam usually have?
faq.a: The median condo that sold in Coquitlam had 2 bedrooms, from the 768 sales between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: Which Coquitlam communities sold the most condos?
faq.a: By number sold: Coquitlam West (389), North Coquitlam (195), New Horizons (59), for November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: Which Coquitlam buildings sold the most condos?
faq.a: By number sold: The Oaks (16), Precidia (15), Lakeside Terrace (14), for November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: What is the benchmark price of a condo in Coquitlam?
faq.a: The Greater Vancouver REALTORS® MLS® Home Price Index benchmark for apartments (condos) in Coquitlam was $640,100 in September 2026, a modelled price for a typical home and not an average of sales.

faq.q: Did condo prices fall in Coquitlam?
faq.a: Over the past year the benchmark fell 7.3%. Over three months it fell 2.1%. A change under 1.5% is not described as a rise or fall.

faq.q: Is Coquitlam a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In October 2026 houses in Coquitlam had a sales ratio of 14%, which the reports’ scale reads as a balanced market, and condos and townhomes 16%, which the reports’ scale reads as a balanced market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos are for sale in Coquitlam?
faq.a: The listing feed on this page shows what is active now, and the number changes daily. Ask Jared and he will send you the condos in Coquitlam that match what you want.

faq.q: Where in Coquitlam should a condo buyer look first?
faq.a: Start with the corridor, not the city. The City's How Development Happens page states growth is focused in transit-oriented areas near SkyTrain — City Centre, Burquitlam and Lougheed take 50% of planned growth — while existing neighbourhoods such as Austin Heights and Maillardville take 29%. That split is why most new condo supply is on Pinetree Way and North Road, and why bench neighbourhoods offer mainly older low-rise stock.

faq.q: How many homes are in The Burquitlam Capital, really?
faq.a: Count it the developer's way, then check the strata plan. The developer, Magusta, records The Burquitlam Capital as 189 condominiums plus four townhomes, 193 homes in total.

faq.q: What will my Coquitlam condo's city tax rate be in 2026?
faq.a: The municipal part is $2.2756 per $1,000 of assessed value. The City's Summary of 2026 Tax Rates sets total municipal Class 1 Residential at $2.2756 per $1,000, made up of $2.1993 for municipal services plus $0.0763 for drainage, with the grand total including other governments at $3.8520 per $1,000. The rate applies the same way to a condo as to a house; the assessed value is what changes the bill.

faq.q: When are Coquitlam taxes and utilities due?
faq.a: Taxes first, utilities earlier in the year. Utility bills were due March 31, 2026. A condo buyer closing mid-year should check both dates on the seller's tax and utility notices, not just the tax certificate.
